location.venue_or_area: Next to Smith Rock State Park; 2025 tent at The Spot at Smith Rock

attendance.note: Organiser-reported: 'Each year we've totaled about 300 people interacting with On This Rock.'

ticket_price.note: Organiser: 'a totally free event' funded by donors and partners (registration required); each edition costs about USD 20,000 to run.

audience.psychographics: Central Oregon climbers of all skill levels at a faith-based gathering focused on accessibility, belonging and 'considering Jesus' approach to spirituality in the climbing space'; climbing films draw locals.

organiser.name: Common Ground (a family of house churches in Central Oregon)

add_sources.note: Google snippet: 'On This Rock Climbing Festival, Oct 10-12' by Common Ground.
29 Oct 2025: 'over 2 weeks since we had our 4th On This Rock Climbing Festival'.
Moved from fall 2026 to spring 2027, 'block out May 21-23, 2027'; 2026 slot ceded to the inaugural Smith Rock Climbing Festival (RedPoint, 2 to 4 Oct 2026).
'a free climbing festival that Common Ground hosts next to Smith Rock State Park in Terrebonne, Oregon'.
FAQ: 'Each year we've totaled about 300 people'; first event 'impacted over 300 people'.
FAQ: 'On This Rock is a totally free event'; events 'cost around $20,000 to put on'.
Mission: improving accessibility, experiencing belonging, considering Jesus' approach to spirituality in climbing.
Bio: 'Exploring Faith & the Outdoors. A family of house churches in Central Oregon. Host of @onthisrockclimbingfest'.
'Have a question, comment, or want to get involved with Common Ground?' Info@commongroundbend.org; donor page commongroundbend.org/donate-to-on-this-rock.

31 Oct 2025: thanks to 'community tabling organizations': Climbers for Christ, RedPoint Climbing, Mountain Supply Oregon, Edelrid, Zigzag Climbing, Smith Rock Group, Escape Climbing (plus a school and an individual).
First Crooked River Crash Bouldering Competition at Smith Rock with prizes; proceeds to local youth climbing clubs.
